title: Broomstick lace handbag
excerpt: A structured handbag in DK yarn using broomstick lace panels. The clustered texture gives body while remaining lightweight, and the bag closes with a simple button.
sourceNotes: A rectangular bag body worked as two broomstick lace panels, seamed together, with a gusset strip and button closure.

glossaryTerms.definition: A narrow strip of crochet sewn along the sides and base of a bag to give it depth and allow it to hold its shape when filled.
A small chain loop attached to the top flap edge that fastens over a button on the bag front to close the bag.

crochet.gaugeText: 3 clusters (15 sts) x 5 rows = 10 cm in broomstick lace on 4.0 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 28 cm wide x 24 cm deep x 8 cm gusset.

on the back panel closes the bag over a button on the front.
Chain 45. Row 1: dc in each ch (45 dc). Broomstick lace in groups of 5 until the panel measures 24 cm. Bind off.

Chain 15. Work dc in each ch, turn, and continue in rows until the strip measures 56 cm (to go around 3 sides of the bag). Sew the gusset to the front panel using the tapestry needle, then attach the back panel.

For each handle, chain 100, slip stitch back along the chain. Attach handles to the top edges. Sew the button to the front panel, 3 cm below the top edge. On the back panel, attach a chain-8 button loop at the centre.
